en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the Philippines.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
Laguna de Bay, located southeast of Metro Manila, is the largest lake in the Philippines.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse marine biodiversity.
The Philippines experiences two main monsoon seasons called amihan, bringing cool northeast winds, and habagat, bringing heavy southwest rains.
The Philippines is a top global producer of abaca, a native banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make ropes.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Batanes islands in the northernmost province of the Philippines feature traditional stone houses built to withstand strong typhoons.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest reserves of nickel, a metal heavily mined in the provinces of Surigao and Palawan.
